stem: After an authorized IPM intervention, old leaf damage remains visible, but new growth is clean, comparable trap counts decline, and no new zones are affected. What is the best conclusion?
choices: The intervention failed because damaged leaves did not recover
The evidence is consistent with improving pressure; continue defined follow-up rather than judging from persistent old damage alone
Discard the trap data because visual damage is always more reliable
rationale: Old tissue can retain damage after causal pressure changes. New growth, comparable trap trends, new signs, and spatial spread are stronger follow-up evidence of current status.
